hindi: तुम उपयाम से ग्रहण किए गए हो; आदित्यों के लिए तुम्हें। हे विष्णु, हे उरुगाय, यह तुम्हारा सोम है; उसकी रक्षा करो; वे तुम्हें हानि न पहुँचाएँ।
english: You are taken with the upayāma; you for the Ādityas. O Viṣṇu, O wide-going one, this is your Soma; guard it; let them not harm you.
notes: upayāma is an obscure ritual term, left untranslated. dabhan is read as a 3 pl. aorist injunctive with prohibitive mā; the subject is not stated. urugāya is rendered as the epithet 'wide-going'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम कभी बाँझ नहीं हो; तुम दाता के प्रति विमुख नहीं होते। हे मघवन्, समीप आओ; अब और अधिक ही तुम्हारा, देव का, दान जुड़ता है। आदित्यों के लिए तुम्हें।
english: O Indra, you are never barren; you do not hold back from the offerer. Come near, O bounteous one; more and more indeed is joined the gift of you, the god. You for the Ādityas.
notes: Obscure: saścasi (taken as 'you hold back', an uncertain sense), the sequence upopennu (read upo upa it nu, uncertain; 'come near' is a guess from upa) and pṛcyate (read 'is joined'; other renderings 'is mingled, abounds'). devasya is taken as 'of the god' with te, without adding an identity. Rendering follows the words as given; confidence is low.

hindi: तुम कभी नहीं चूकते; तुम दोनों जन्मों की रक्षा करते हो। हे आदित्य, चौथा सवन तुम्हारा है; तुम्हारा बल अमर रूप में स्वर्ग में स्थित हुआ है। आदित्यों के लिए तुम्हें।
english: You never neglect; you protect both births. The fourth pressing is yours, O Āditya; your power has taken its stand, immortal, in heaven. You for the Ādityas.
notes: turīya 'fourth' is taken as agreeing with savana, and the sentence is read as 'the fourth pressing is yours'; this is uncertain. amṛtam may be a noun ('the immortal') rather than an adjective. 'both births' is the literal janmanī.

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pres. part. caus. √mṛḍ

hindi: देवों का यज्ञ अनुग्रह की ओर जाता है; हे आदित्यो, प्रसन्न करते हुए कृपालु बनो। तुम्हारी हमारी ओर मुड़ी हुई सुमति यहाँ लौट आए, जो संकट से भी विस्तृत स्थान को अधिक पाने वाली हो। आदित्यों के लिए तुम्हें।
english: The sacrifice of the gods goes towards favour; O Ādityas, be gracious, showing kindness. May your favour, turned towards us, come back hither, that which would be, even out of distress, the better finder of wide room. You for the Ādityas.

text_flags.why: possible: the word ahoḥ is not otherwise known; parallel texts read aṃhoḥ 'distress', so the anusvāra may be missing

notes: Reading of ahoḥ/aṃhoḥ as 'distress' is uncertain. varivovit-tarā is read as 'more finding wide room' (variva- = wide space, freedom); alternatives exist. vo is taken as vaḥ 'your' with sumati.

words.gloss: the two lords of the house

hindi: हे विवस्वान्, हे आदित्य, यह तुम्हारा सोमपान है; उसमें आनन्द लो। हे मनुष्यो, इस वचन में श्रद्धा रखो: जब आशीर्वाद देने वाले दम्पती वांछित को प्राप्त करते हैं, तब पुरुष पुत्र उत्पन्न होता है, वह धन पाता है और तब निर्दोष होकर प्रतिदिन घर में समृद्ध होता है।
english: O Vivasvat, O Āditya, this is your soma-drinking; delight in it. O men, place your trust in this speech: when the two lords of the house, bestowers of blessing, obtain the desirable, a male son is born, he finds wealth, and then, faultless, he thrives in the house every day.
notes: Line 2 is hard: 'yad āśīrdā dampatī vāmam aśnutaḥ' is rendered with yad as 'when', āśīrdā as an adjective of the pair ('bestowers of blessing') and vāma as 'the desirable'; the construction is uncertain. The text speaks of 'the two lords of the house' (dampatī) without naming them; arapaḥ is read 'faultless' (a-rapas). Vivasvat and Āditya are two vocatives as printed and are not further identified.

hindi: हे सविता, आज हमें प्रिय धन दो, कल भी, और दिन-प्रतिदिन प्रिय धन दो। क्योंकि हे देव, प्रिय निवास के, प्रचुर के, इस बुद्धि से हम प्रिय के भागी हों।
english: O Savitṛ, give us today the precious thing, and tomorrow too, and day by day give us the precious thing. For, O god, of the precious abode, of the abundant, by this thought may we be sharers of the precious.
notes: vāma 'precious, desirable thing' is rendered as 'the precious thing'. dive dive is read as 'day by day' (a reduplicated dative idiom). The last clause is elliptical; the genitives vāmasya kṣayasya bhūreḥ depend on the sharing in an uncertain way.

hindi: तुम उपयाम से ग्रहण किए गए हो, तुम सावित्र हो, तुम अन्न देने वाले हो, अन्न देने वाले हो; मुझमें अन्न स्थापित करो। यज्ञ को प्रेरित करो, यज्ञपति को प्रेरित करो। भग के लिए, देव सविता के लिए तुम्हें।
english: You are taken with the upayāma; you are Sāvitra; you are a bestower of food, a bestower of food; place food in me. Quicken the sacrifice, quicken the lord of the sacrifice. You for Bhaga, for the god Savitṛ.
notes: canodhāḥ (canas 'food, satisfaction') is repeated as printed. bhagāya devāya savitre may be read as 'for Bhaga, for the god Savitṛ' or 'for the god Savitṛ the giver (bhaga)'; the first, literal reading is used. Sāvitra is rendered 'belonging to Savitṛ'.

hindi: तुम उपयाम से ग्रहण किए गए हो, तुम उत्तम आश्रय वाले हो, भली-भाँति प्रतिष्ठित हो; महान वृषभ को नमस्कार। सब देवों के लिए तुम्हें। यह तुम्हारी योनि है। सब देवों के लिए तुम्हें।
english: You are taken with the upayāma; you are of good shelter, well established; homage to the great bull. You for all the gods. This is your womb. You for all the gods.
notes: bṛhadukṣāya is taken as a dative 'to the great bull' (ukṣan); the form with -a is as printed. yoni is rendered 'womb' (its literal sense); it may mean 'seat, source' in context.

words.gloss: of the one pressed by Bṛhaspati

hindi: तुम उपयाम से ग्रहण किए गए हो। हे देव सोम, बृहस्पति द्वारा निचोड़े गए तुम्हारे बिन्दु के बलयुक्त और पत्नियों वाले ग्रहों को मैं पाकर समृद्ध होऊँ। मैं ऊपर से हूँ, मैं नीचे से हूँ; जो अन्तरिक्ष है, वही मेरा पिता हुआ। मैंने सूर्य को दोनों ओर से देखा; मैंने देवों के उस परम को देखा जो गुहा में है।
english: You are taken with the upayāma. O god Soma, of you, the drop pressed by Bṛhaspati, may I prosper in the cups that have power and are accompanied by wives. I am from above, I am from below; what is the midspace, that became my father. I saw Sūrya on both sides; I saw the highest of the gods, which is in secret.
notes: Obscure in several places. bṛhaspatisutasya is taken as 'of the one pressed by Bṛhaspati', agreeing with indoḥ/Soma; ta indor is read te indoḥ 'of you, the drop'. ṛdhyāsam with accusative grahān is read as 'may I prosper in/through' (uncertain construction); the mark ~2 on grahān is a printed nasal/length sign. Line 3, 'devānāṃ paramaṃ guhā yat', is read 'the highest of the gods, which is in secret' (aham dadarśa governs it). Antarikṣa is rendered 'midspace'.

hindi: हे अग्नि, पत्नियों वाले, देव त्वष्टा के साथ मिलकर सोम पियो। स्वाहा। तुम प्रजापति हो, वृषभ हो, बीज स्थापित करने वाले हो; मुझमें बीज स्थापित करो। प्रजापति के, तुम वृषभ के, बीज स्थापित करने वाले के बीज-स्थापन को मैं प्राप्त करूँ।
english: O Agni, O one accompanied by wives, united with the god Tvaṣṭṛ, drink the Soma. Svāhā. You are Prajāpati, a bull, a placer of seed; place seed in me. May I obtain the seed-placing of you, of Prajāpati, the bull, the placer of seed.
notes: agnā3i is read as agne with a prolongation (pluta) mark. 'prajāpatir vṛṣā'si' could be 'you are Prajāpati, a bull' or 'Prajāpati, you are a bull'; the first is used. retodhām is read as a noun 'the placing of seed' (uncertain).

hindi: तुम उपयाम से ग्रहण किए गए हो, तुम भूरे रंग के हो, हारियोजन हो; दोनों भूरे अश्वों के लिए तुम्हें। तुम दोनों भूरों के भुने दाने हो, सोम के साथ, इन्द्र के लिए।
english: You are taken with the upayāma; you are tawny; you are Hāriyojana; you for the two bays. You are the grains of the two bays, together with Soma, for Indra.
notes: hāriyojana is an obscure term, kept as printed. hari is rendered 'tawny, bay' (the colour word); haribhyām and haryoḥ are read as 'the two bays' (a pair of bay ones); the text does not say what they are. dhānā is read 'grains'.

hindi: तुम्हारा जो अश्व देने वाला भक्ष है, जो गौ देने वाला है, उस तुम्हारे, जिसका यजुः इष्ट है, जिसका सोम स्तुत है, जिसका उक्थ शंसित है, जो आहूत है, उस तुम्हारे भक्ष को मैं, आहूत होकर, खाता हूँ।
english: Your draught that wins horses, that wins cows: of you, of that kind, whose yajus is desired, whose Soma is praised, whose recitation is recited, who are invoked, I, invoked, partake.
notes: Obscure. aśvasani and gosani are read 'winning horses / winning cows'. iṣṭayajuṣaḥ (iṣṭa = desired or offered) is uncertain. The genitive chain describes te; upahūtasya upahūtaḥ is read as 'of the invoked one, I the invoked'. bhakṣayāmi is read 'I partake' (denominative of bhakṣa).

hindi: तुम देवों द्वारा किए गए पाप का प्रायश्चित्त हो; तुम मनुष्यों द्वारा किए गए पाप का प्रायश्चित्त हो; तुम पितरों द्वारा किए गए पाप का प्रायश्चित्त हो; तुम स्वयं किए गए पाप का प्रायश्चित्त हो; तुम पाप-पाप का प्रायश्चित्त हो। और जो पाप मैंने जानते हुए किया, और जो अनजाने में किया, उस सब पाप का तुम प्रायश्चित्त हो।
english: You are the expiation of the sin made by the gods; you are the expiation of the sin made by men; you are the expiation of the sin made by the fathers; you are the expiation of the sin made by oneself; you are the expiation of sin upon sin. And whatever sin I have done knowing, and whatever not knowing, of all that sin you are the expiation.
notes: avayajana (ava-yajana) is rendered 'expiation' (literally a sacrificing-away). enasa enaso is read 'of sin upon sin'. 'yac cāham eno vidvāṃś cakāra yac cāvidvāṃs tasya' is read as 'the sin which I did knowing, and which not knowing, of that'. The mark ~ on vidvā~ś and avidvā~s is a printed nasal sign. The English of the last sentence follows the Sanskrit order.

hindi: हम तेज के साथ, दूध के साथ, शरीरों के साथ, मन के साथ, कल्याणकारी के साथ मिल गए हैं। उदार दाता त्वष्टा धन का वितरण करें, और शरीर का जो ढीला-बिछुड़ा है, उसे पोंछकर ठीक करें।
english: We have come together with splendour, with milk, with bodies, with mind, with the kind one. May Tvaṣṭṛ, the generous giver, distribute riches, and may he wipe over whatever is loosened of the body.
notes: saṃ ... aganmahi is read with all the instrumentals; śivena is taken as a noun-adjective 'the kind (one)' and could agree with manasā ('with a kindly mind'); the second reading is also natural. viliṣṭam is obscure ('loosened, misjoined'). payas is rendered 'milk' (could be 'fluid, juice'). Unit 16 repeats this text.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हमें मन से, गौओं से, संरक्षकों से, हे मघवन्, और कल्याण से मिलाओ; ब्रह्मन् से और जो देवों द्वारा किया हुआ है उससे मिलाओ; यज्ञ के योग्य देवों की सुमति में मिलाओ। स्वाहा।
english: O Indra, bring us together with mind, with cows, with patrons, O bounteous one, with well-being; together with brahman, and with whatever is made by the gods; together in the favour of the gods worthy of sacrifice. Svāhā.
notes: sam ... neṣi is read as 'unite us', and the repeated sam as continuing it. sūri is rendered 'patron' (also 'wise man'); brahmaṇā is the neuter brahman (sacred formula or prayer), left as 'brahman'. 'devakṛtaṃ yad asti' is read as 'whatever is made by the gods'.

hindi: हम तेज के साथ, दूध के साथ, शरीरों के साथ, मन के साथ, कल्याणकारी के साथ मिल गए हैं। उदार दाता त्वष्टा धन का वितरण करें, और शरीर का जो ढीला-बिछुड़ा है, उसे पोंछकर ठीक करें।
english: We have come together with splendour, with milk, with bodies, with mind, with the kind one. May Tvaṣṭṛ, the generous giver, distribute riches, and may he wipe over whatever is loosened of the body.
notes: GROUPING: the text is identical to unit 14 (repeated in the edition); both units kept as given. saṃ ... aganmahi is read with all the instrumentals; śivena is taken as a noun-adjective 'the kind (one)' and could agree with manasā ('with a kindly mind'); the second reading is also natural. viliṣṭam is obscure ('loosened, misjoined'). payas is rendered 'milk' (could be 'fluid, juice').

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pf. part. mid. sam-√rā

hindi: धाता, राति और सविता इसका सेवन करें; प्रजापति, निधि के रक्षक, देव अग्नि भी। त्वष्टा और विष्णु, सन्तान के साथ दान करते हुए, यजमान को धन प्रदान करो। स्वाहा।
english: May Dhātṛ, Rāti, Savitṛ enjoy this, and Prajāpati, the guardian of treasure, the god Agni. O Tvaṣṭṛ, O Viṣṇu, bestowing together with offspring, grant wealth to the sacrificer. Svāhā.
notes: Dhātṛ and Rāti are kept as names; rāti means 'gift' and may not be a personal name here. nidhipāḥ is taken with Prajāpati as printed (prajāpatir nidhipā), but could be a separate title. dadhāta is a plural imperative, so tvaṣṭā viṣṇuḥ are read as addressed together with the others; the text gives no further identification. saṃrarāṇāḥ is read 'bestowing together' (uncertain sense).

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pres. part. mid. √juṣ
m. nom. pl. pres. part. mid. √bhṛ
m. nom. pl. pres. part. mid. √vah

hindi: हे देवो, हमने तुम्हारे लिए सुगम आसन बनाए हैं, तुम जो इस सवन में आनन्द लेते हुए आए हो। हवियाँ लाते हुए, वहन करते हुए, हे वसुओ, हमें धन दो। स्वाहा।
english: O gods, we have made easy seats for you, you who have come to this pressing, enjoying it. Bearing and carrying the oblations, O Vasus, give us wealth. Svāhā.
notes: sugā is read as 'easy to go (to)', agreeing with sadanā. vasūni is rendered 'wealth, goods'; vasavaḥ is kept as 'Vasus' (a class of gods named in the line).

words.gram: m. acc. pl. (with printed nasal mark)

hindi: जिन उत्सुक देवों को तुम बुलाते हो, हे देव, उन देवों को हे अग्नि, अपने साथ के आसन में प्रेरित करो। भोजन कर चुके और पी चुके तुम सब प्राण पर, घर्म पर, स्वर्ग पर क्रम से आरूढ़ हो जाओ। स्वाहा।
english: Whichever eager gods you bring hither, O god, those gods send forth, O Agni, in your own common seat. All of you who have eaten and drunk, mount the life-breath, the hot offering, heaven, in turn. Svāhā.

text_flags.why: typo: Latin letter j typed for the anusvāra (the Devanagari line also has j), the perfect participle is papivāṃsaḥ

notes: yā~2 is yān with a printed nasal/length mark. The construction of line 1 is uncertain: āvaha (imperative) with yān ... tān is rendered as a relative clause. In line 2 the objects of ātiṣṭhata (asum, gharmam, svar) and the sense of anu 'in turn, after' are uncertain; asu is rendered 'life-breath', gharma 'heat, hot offering'. sve ... sadhasthe is read 'in your own common seat' (uncertain).

words.gram: m. loc. sg. pres. part. pra-√i
m. nom. sg. pres. part. pra-√jñā

hindi: हे अग्नि, हमने तुम्हें यहाँ इस चल रहे यज्ञ में होता चुना है। अलग-अलग इस प्रकार तुमने परिश्रम किया है; भली-भाँति जानते हुए, जानने वाले तुम यज्ञ के पास जाओ। स्वाहा।
english: For we chose you here, O Agni, as hotṛ in this sacrifice that is under way. Separately by this, separately you have toiled; knowing well, knowing, go to the sacrifice. Svāhā.
notes: Line 2 is obscure: 'ṛdhag ayā ṛdhag utāśamiṣṭhāḥ' is rendered literally ('separately by this, separately you have toiled'); aśamiṣṭhāḥ is read as an aorist of √śam 'toil'. The sense is uncertain. prayati is read as a participle 'being undertaken'.

hindi: हे देवो, मार्ग खोजने वालो, मार्ग पाकर मार्ग पर चलो। हे मन के स्वामी, हे देव, इस यज्ञ को वायु में स्थापित करो। स्वाहा।
english: O gods, finders of the way, having found the way, go on the way. O lord of the mind, O god, place this sacrifice in the wind. Svāhā.
notes: The second svāhā and the order 'svāhā vāte dhāḥ' are as printed; svāhā is read as a formula inserted before the verb. manasaspati is read as 'lord of the mind' (manasas-pati).

words.gloss: with the sūkta and the utterance

hindi: हे यज्ञ, यज्ञ के पास जाओ, यज्ञपति के पास जाओ, अपनी योनि में जाओ। स्वाहा। हे यज्ञपति, यह तुम्हारा यज्ञ है, सूक्त और वाक् सहित, सब वीरों सहित; उसका सेवन करो। स्वाहा।
english: O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice, go to the lord of the sacrifice, go to your own womb. Svāhā. This is your sacrifice, O lord of the sacrifice, with the sūkta and the utterance, with all heroes; enjoy it. Svāhā.
notes: sahasūktavākaḥ is read as saha-sūkta-vākaḥ 'with sūkta and utterance' (uncertain; other splits exist). yoni is rendered 'womb, source'.

hindi: साँप मत बनो, पृदाकु मत बनो। राजा वरुण ने सूर्य के अनुसरण के लिए विस्तृत मार्ग बनाया। उसने पाँवरहित के लिए पाँव रखने को पाँव बनाए, और हृदय को बेधने वालों का भी निन्दक बनाया। वरुण को नमस्कार। वरुण का पाश खड़ा है।
english: Do not be a snake, do not be a pṛdāku. King Varuṇa made a wide path for the sun to follow. For the footless he made feet to set down, and a rebuker even of the heart-piercers. Homage to Varuṇa. Varuṇa's noose stands set.
notes: The pause mark | is a separate token as printed. pṛdāku is kept (an obscure animal name). Line 2 is obscure: akaḥ is the 3 sg. aorist 'he made'; apavaktā is read 'rebuker, one who speaks against'; 'he made a rebuker even of the heart-piercers' is a literal rendering of an unclear clause. abhiṣṭhitaḥ is read 'stands set (over)'; no object is stated.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. prati-√rakṣ

hindi: अग्नि का अग्रभाग जलों में प्रविष्ट हुआ; अपां नपात असुर-सम्बन्धी बल की रक्षा करता हुआ। प्रत्येक घर में हे अग्नि, तुम समिधा अर्पित करते हो; तुम्हारी जिह्वा की ओर घी ऊपर चलता हुआ। स्वाहा।
english: The face of Agni has entered the waters, Apām Napāt guarding the lordly power. In every house you offer kindling, O Agni; towards your tongue the ghee moves upward. Svāhā.
notes: apāṃ napāt is kept as 'Apām Napāt' (literally 'son of the waters'). asurya is rendered 'lordly power' (a-sura-ya, uncertain). yakṣi samidham is read 'you offer kindling'. ghṛtam uccaraṇyat is obscure and the sentence is incomplete as printed.

words.gloss: in the saying of the sūkta

hindi: समुद्र में तुम्हारा हृदय है, जलों के भीतर। तुममें ओषधियाँ और जल प्रविष्ट हों। हे यज्ञपति, यज्ञ के सूक्त-कथन में और नमः-वाक् में हम तुम्हारी सेवा करें, जो कुछ भी। स्वाहा।
english: In the ocean is your heart, within the waters. May plants and waters enter you. O lord of the sacrifice, in the saying of the sūkta and the utterance of homage of the sacrifice, may we serve you, whatever it be. Svāhā.
notes: yajñasya is read with the two locatives ('of the sacrifice'). yat svāhā is read 'whatever it be'; the use of yat is uncertain. oṣadhi is rendered 'plant'.

hindi: हे दिव्य जलो, यह तुम्हारा गर्भ है; उसे भली-भाँति प्रसन्न, भली-भाँति धारित करके धारण करो। हे देव सोम, यह तुम्हारा लोक है; उसमें कल्याणकारी होकर बढ़ो और चारों ओर बढ़ो।
english: O divine waters, this is your embryo; bear him, well pleased and well borne. O god Soma, this is your world; in it grow with well-being and grow all around.
notes: vakṣva is read as an imperative of √vakṣ 'grow, be strong'; it could also be √vah 'carry' (vakṣva as future-imperative), which would give 'bear well-being and bear around'. The first reading is used (uncertain). devīr āpaḥ is read as a vocative address; the embryo is not identified.

hindi: हे अवभृथ, हे निचुम्पुण, तुम निचेरु हो, निचुम्पुण। देवों के साथ मैंने देवों द्वारा किए गए पाप को दूर किया; मनुष्यों के साथ मनुष्यों द्वारा किए गए पाप को दूर किया। हे पुरुरावन् के देव, हानि से रक्षा करो। तुम देवों की समिधा हो।
english: O avabhṛtha, O Nicumpuṇa, you are nicēru, Nicumpuṇa. With the gods I have appeased the sin made by the gods; with mortals the sin made by mortals. O god of Pururāvan, protect from harm. You are the kindling-stick of the gods.
notes: Very obscure: nicumpuṇa, nicēru and pururāvṇaḥ are kept untranslated (pururāvṇo deva is rendered 'O god of Pururāvan', uncertain). ayāsiṣam (ava-√yā) is read 'I have appeased'; other renderings are 'I have averted, removed'. avabhṛtha is the final bath (a ritual term kept as 'avabhṛtha'). samit is read 'kindling-stick' (samidh).

hindi: दस मास का गर्भ जरायु के साथ हिले। जैसे यह वायु चलती है, जैसे समुद्र हिलता है, वैसे ही यह दस मास का गर्भ जरायु के साथ छूटा।
english: Let the ten-month embryo move together with the afterbirth. As this wind moves, as the ocean moves, so this ten-month one was released together with the afterbirth.
notes: asraj is read as a form of √sṛj 'was released' (the exact form, aorist passive or injunctive, is uncertain). The word and the line break after 'saha' are as printed. The subject is the embryo as stated; nothing more is added.

hindi: जिसके लिए तुम्हारा यज्ञ के योग्य गर्भ है, जिसके लिए सुनहरी योनि है; जिसके अंग अवक्र हैं, उसे मैंने माता से मिला दिया है। स्वाहा।
english: She for whom your embryo is worthy of sacrifice, for whom the womb is golden; him whose limbs are unbent I have united with his mother. Svāhā.
notes: yasyai is a dative form of the relative (the construction 'to whom ... the embryo' is read loosely as 'she for whom'). ahrutā is read 'unbent, not crooked' (a-hruta), uncertain. The text does not say who the mother or the embryo is.

hindi: बहुत आश्चर्यों वाला, नाना रूपों वाला, बिन्दु, धीर, भीतर महिमा को आलिप्त कर चुका है। एकपदी, द्विपदी, त्रिपदी, चतुष्पदी, अष्टापदी लोकों में फैलें। स्वाहा।
english: Rich in wonders, of various forms, the drop, the wise one has anointed the greatness within. May the one-footed, the two-footed, the three-footed, the four-footed, the eight-footed spread along the worlds. Svāhā.
notes: Obscure. ānañja is read 'has anointed' (ā-√añj), with mahimānam as object; the sense 'has made manifest' is also possible. induḥ is rendered 'drop'. The five feminine numerals (ekapadī ... aṣṭāpadī) are accusative as printed but the verb prathantām is plural imperative, so they are read as its subjects; what they refer to is not stated and is not added.

hindi: हे मरुतो, स्वर्ग के महान तेज वाले, जिसके निवास में तुम रक्षा करते हो, वह मनुष्य सर्वोत्तम रक्षित है।
english: O Maruts of heaven, of great glory, he in whose dwelling you give protection is the best protected man.
notes: pāthā is read as √pā 'protect'; √pā 'drink' is also possible ('in whose dwelling you drink'). divaḥ is read 'of heaven' with vimahasaḥ. The quality of the order of the clause is as printed.

hindi: महान द्यौ और पृथ्वी हमारे इस यज्ञ को सींचें; अपने पोषणों से हमें भरपूर करें।
english: May great heaven and earth sprinkle this our sacrifice; may they fill us with their nourishments.
notes: mimikṣatām is read 'may they sprinkle, moisten' (desiderative of √mikṣ, uncertain). bharīman is rendered 'nourishment' (bearing, bringing). mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca is read as two nouns with a dual adjective.
